newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Euroyen, JGB futures unmoved by Nikkei surge.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Euroyen, JGB futures unmoved by Nikkei surge.

text.p: SIMEX Euroyen and Japanese government bond (JGB) futures traded sluggishly on Monday, shrugging off a sharp rise in Tokyo stocks as players remained keen to buy on any dips.
The 225-share Nikkei average ended up 353.23 points to 20,228.72, boosted by active buying of high technology shares.
Comments by the Liberal Democratic Party's top policymaker, Taku Yamasaki, that the Nikkei was likely to reach 21,000 by the end of the summer contributed to the rally, dealers said.
"The Nikkei went shooting up. But the Euroyen didn't really react to it," a trader at a European futures house said.
He said the lead March contract dipped to its day low of 98.99 after a key Japanese business leader said Japan may need to change its credit policy.

Shoichiro Toyoda, chairman of the business lobby Keidanren, told a news conference Japan's current low interest rate policy may need to be changed a bit in order to make it more balanced with those of other nations.
But the impact on the interest rate market was limited as most participants remain confident Japan will not raise rates in the foreseeable future, the dealer said.
"I'm looking for higher levels in the Euroyen. March could go back to 99.05," he said.
The contract stood at 99.00 at 1115 GMT against its IMM close at 99.01 on volume of 7,162 lots.
September JGBs ended at 124.88 against a previous 124.85.
Eurodollar futures ended flat after an even more subdued session ahead of the U.S. June retail sales report, due on Tuesday.
December Eurodollars ended unchanged at 94.070 against its previous IMM close on volume of 4,360 lots.
